info.text:
Americans added about $28 billion of consumer debt in September.
Revolving credit, mostly credit cards, grew at a 14.5% annual pace in September after shrinking 4.4% in August (Fed G.19, Nov 6, 2026).
Revolving balances reached $1.369 trillion, and cards made up more than half of the month's increase.
The average rate on cards charging interest was 22.36% in Q3. Our math: $1,000 carried a year is roughly $224 in interest.
Sources: Federal Reserve G.19 (Nov 6, 2026) via PYMNTS, Investing.com, LendingTree.
News and education, not financial advice.
